newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extends up trend.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extends up trend.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were firm around midday on Tuesday, despite weaker overnight crude, as tight regional supplies underpinned the recent rally, market sources said.
December gas oil swaps edged up in early trading with one lot traded at $30.85 per barrel, up from late Monday's $30.65/$30.75. December was last quoted at $30.75/$30.95, brokers said.
"Supplies are tight for December and the Chinese are buying prompt cargoes," one trader said.
With the increased buying from China and other regional buyers, such as Indonesia, Singapore physical premiums have risen to about 50 cents above spot quotes from 30 cents in the past two weeks.
Traders said Singapore refiners have in the past few days sold some export cargoes around 50 cents above spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Overnight, January Brent crude futures in London fell 41 cents a barrel to $22.61 on news Iraq had agreed to all the conditions for the United Nations oil-for-food deal.
Gas oil futures, traded in London, also lost ground. December futures dropped $3.75 a tonne to $219.00.
Jet fuel swaps were cautious with buyers reducing bids for December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) to about $2.00 per barrel, down from Monday's $2.60/$2.80 a barrel, brokers said.
Nevertheless traders said the market remained firm and they expected the regrade to pick up later in the day. December jet fuel swaps were quoted at $32.80/$33.20, brokers said.
The recent up trend on jet fuel was due to traders covering earlier sale commitments to North Asia, industry sources said.
Naphtha opened down slightly at midday due to the weaker crude with December quoted at $23.30/$23.60, from Monday's $23.50/$23.70, brokers said.
Fuel oil was quoted unchanged from Monday as the market continues to see buying support from local traders. December was last quoted at $120.00/$120.75.
